title: Add nightly quant-perf canary (FP8/INT8) with thresholds + Slack alerts
author: Sahana Iyer
body:
Context: As part of the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint, we need a repeatable canary that catches regressions in quantized execution paths (both kernel-level perf and end-to-end serving metrics) before they ship broadly. This PR adds a new nightly GitHub Actions workflow that runs a reduced, stable quant-perf matrix on selected GPUs, compares results against pinned baselines, and posts pass/fail summaries to Slack (#eng-runtime) with links to artifacts.

What this adds: (1) A new workflow: `.github/workflows/quant-perf-nightly.yml` scheduled nightly (03:15 UTC) and runnable manually via `workflow_dispatch` with inputs for `gpu_sku`, `quant_mode`, and `matrix_profile`. (2) A new canary job type `quant-perf` that invokes the benchmark runner, produces a normalized results JSON, and uploads it as an artifact with consistent metadata tags (gpu_sku, quant_mode, model_family, runtime_commit, container_digest, cuda_version). (3) Threshold-based gating: define pass/fail criteria for TTFT p95, TPOT p95, and decode tokens/sec (phase-split) using a simple comparator against the stored baseline. Default thresholds are intentionally conservative for week 1 (block only large regressions; alert on smaller deltas). (4) Slack notifications: a summary message per GPU/quant mode, plus a thread with the worst offenders and a link to the full report artifact; includes a "rerun" hint and the run ID.

Initial matrix (kept small to reduce noise and perf-lab contention): GPUs: `A100-80GB` and `H100-SXM` (H200 and L40S are intentionally not enabled until infra capacity is confirmed). Quant modes: `fp8` and `int8`. Workloads: (a) prefill-heavy (long prompt, short decode) and (b) decode-heavy (short prompt, longer decode), each at two concurrency points. Models: one representative Llama-family and one Qwen-family profile (model names are abstracted in config to avoid churn; the runner pulls actual IDs from the pinned benchmark config).

Baselines: Baseline JSON files are committed under `baselines/quant-perf/<gpu_sku>/<quant_mode>.json` and reference a pinned runtime commit + container digest. The workflow will refuse to compare if metadata indicates a drifted environment (e.g., different CUDA driver major) unless `ALLOW_ENV_DRIFT=true` is set on manual runs.

Operational details / safety: (1) The workflow is marked `concurrency: quant-perf-nightly` to avoid overlapping runs. (2) Timeouts are set per phase to fail fast when nodes are unhealthy. (3) Slack uses `SLACK_WEBHOOK_ENG_RUNTIME` secret; messages are suppressed on forks.

Why this approach: we want a small, stable, high-signal canary that runs every night and alerts quickly. The full sprint benchmark matrix stays in benchmark-lab and is too heavy/noisy for continuous gating.

Follow-ups: Comparator robustness and outlier handling will be improved in a subsequent PR (see discussion; we’ll likely move to trimmed mean + median-of-means and add retry-on-first-failure). H200/L40S enablement will be gated on INT-842 capacity work and a stable image pin.

Testing: `act` dry-run for workflow syntax; local run of `canary run --job quant-perf --gpu A100-80GB --quant fp8` against a staging runner; validated Slack formatting in #eng-runtime-test.

Release notes: Adds nightly quant-perf canary coverage for FP8/INT8 on A100/H100 with Slack alerting and baseline comparison thresholds.
commits: ci: add nightly quant-perf workflow with schedule + manual dispatch
canary: implement quant-perf runner wrapper and results normalization
baselines: add initial A100/H100 FP8/INT8 baseline files
alerts: Slack notifier for quant-perf summary + worst regressions
docs: add runbook section for reruns and baseline updates
review_conversation: Connor O'Brien: Can we ensure this doesn’t block release trains yet? I’m ok with alert-only for week 1; let’s avoid hard failures on small deltas. Also please add a link in the Slack message to the baseline commit.

Sahana Iyer: Updated thresholds to: fail only if TTFT p95 regresses >12% or TPOT p95 >10% or tok/s drops >10%. Added an "alert" tier at 5% that doesn’t fail the workflow. Slack now includes baseline commit + runtime commit in the header.
Sean Gallagher: Concerned about perf-lab contention and noisy nodes. Can we add concurrency control and a node-health preflight (GPU clocks + no MIG) so we don’t page ourselves every night?

Sahana Iyer: Added `concurrency: quant-perf-nightly` and a preflight step that checks GPU name, MIG disabled, persistence mode, and prints application clocks; workflow aborts with "infra" classification and tags the Slack message accordingly.
Allison Grant: Please tag Slack messages with gpu_sku + quant_mode consistently so we can route/aggregate later. Also add a JSON payload attachment with deltas for dashboards.
Sahana Iyer: Added tags `gpu=<...> quant=<...> job=quant-perf` in Slack text and included a compact JSON block (top regressions) as a threaded message; full JSON remains as artifact for ingestion.

Noah Patel: The metadata drift guard is good, but make sure manual dispatch can bypass it for investigations. Also please split prefill vs decode metrics in the comparator; TTFT should be treated separately from decode tok/s.
Sahana Iyer: Manual dispatch now supports `ALLOW_ENV_DRIFT` and comparator reports per-phase: prefill TTFT p95 + decode tok/s + TPOT p95. Added phase labels to results JSON.
outcome_summary: Merged. Nightly quant-perf workflow enabled on main for A100-80GB and H100-SXM (FP8 + INT8). Slack alerts go to #eng-runtime with artifact links and baseline/runtime metadata. Fail thresholds are conservative; smaller deltas are alert-only.
release_notes: New nightly quant-perf canary for FP8/INT8 on A100/H100
Baseline comparison with conservative pass/fail thresholds (TTFT/TPOT/tok/s)
Slack notifications with artifact links and environment metadata
